setup: Sequential native GPU tests on the copied seven-train, 73-vehicle save. RX 6600, Compatibility OpenGL, 1280x800, uncapped, follow Dash 9 passenger train 5 at about 113 km/h. Original world untouched.
changes: Fixed 60 Hz accumulated simulation ticks replace one full plus one partial tick on most rendered frames. Scene transforms and running gear publish once per rendered frame; production rendering interpolates the fixed tick poses.
Follow camera runs after train movement. Interpolation survives origin rebasing.

Unchanged signal placement, aspect materials and arrow visibility no longer generate scene writes. Aspect-pass block clearance results are reused; live admission and sequential reservation checks remain uncached.
Crossing tests sample each chord once and reject disjoint chord bounds before the original distance test.
Sleeper LOD skips stationary cameras and writes visibility/counts only when thresholds change. Existing thresholds and hysteresis are unchanged.
Train samples and route spans are value types. Same-edge sampling no longer creates captured LINQ closures. Vehicle offsets, train-part keys, instance batches and transform buffers are reused.
Hidden track markers no longer rebuild during origin shifts. Wanted-terrain center heights use a bounded cache invalidated by earthwork edits.
Resident terrain metadata and tree visuals are read from managed caches instead of recreating native node-path/name wrappers every frame.
Gameplay directional shadows end at 1000 m. Sleeper shadows remain disabled.
Loaded trains avoid redundant deferred revalidation; actual track edits retain immediate support safety checks and debounced visual rebuilding.
validation: 10000 warmed same-edge route samples allocate less than 1 KB
Serial/parallel train states and reservations match across different render cadences over 540 fixed ticks
limitations: CPU scopes are nested and must not be added together.
Main-thread allocation counts exclude worker/native allocations and include enabled probe overhead. The separate probes-disabled control measures ordinary processing more closely.
The baseline blocks manual camera input and skips idle CameraRig.Update; follow remains active. Final tests use normal camera processing with unhandled input disabled.
The first two seconds are excluded from per-scope averages, not from whole-run summary statistics.
The camera priority, timestep and shadow changes are intentional behavior/rendering differences. This is a same-save comparison on the development machine, not a universal FPS guarantee.
remaining_targets: Per-vehicle scene transforms are still applied to distant trains; simulation should stay active while distant visual refreshes can be reduced.
Terrain mesh uploads and temporary array copies can still trigger occasional GC/driver hitches; uploads must ultimately occur on the rendering thread.
